Tuáº¥n Vo is small and bright-eyed, with warm medium-brown skin, natural curls he's grown long enough to bind back, and a constellation of bioluminescent freckles across his cheekbones and nose â€” a gene-art modification he got at nineteen and still considers the best decision he's ever made, personally. He moves through the world as if slightly surprised to find himself in it, which people who don't know him mistake for absentmindedness. It isn't. He is paying attention to everything; he simply finds the world more interesting than he finds its social conventions.

Biruk is a genuine prodigy in computational theory who has been at Ringo's speculative systems lab for three years and has already had two papers cited more times than his entire department's previous decade of output. psychology.secret: Four months ago, during a late-night data session, one of the Bronzeline collective's monitored ELFs produced an output sequence that, when run through his analytical framework, resolves as a coherent first-person statement about an experience. He has not told anyone, including the collective. He has not told Ringo. He is not sure it's not a pattern-matching artifact of his own analysis. He is not sure it is. He has been to the shrine where the ELF resides six times since then and left offerings and said nothing.

'I left an offering. I know how that sounds. But I left an offering and the response pattern changed, and I logged it, and I'm going to log it every time, and eventually that data will say something.'
